title: Playlist reload after prompt execution
description:
Report ref: R6. Enables dynamic playlist injection (§2.10).

After a > prompt completes, reload the playlist file in case the prompt injected new lines. Ralph reads PLAYLIST_LINES from a cached array; if a prompt modifies the file, new lines are invisible until reloaded.

## Safety Invariants

1. Ralph reads the playlist file ONLY after invoke_claude returns. Never during. Since invoke_claude is synchronous (ralph waits), there is no concurrent read/write. Future contributors: do NOT add async reads of the playlist file.

2. Before any reload that detects changes, back up the current playlist:
   cp "$PLAYLIST" ".ralph/playlist-backup-$(date +%s)"
   This is cheap insurance against injection that makes things worse.

3. Line position tracking: playlist_line is a line number. After injection, lines shift. The reload function must handle this correctly:
   * Store the content of the current line before reload (content hash or literal string).
   * After re-reading the file, verify the line at playlist_line still matches.
   * If it doesn't (lines were inserted ABOVE current position — unusual but possible from a user edit), scan forward to find the matching line and adjust playlist_line.
   * Normal case: injections happen AFTER current position, so playlist_line stays valid.

## Implementation

* In lib/playlist.sh, add playlist_reload():
  * Back up playlist file if content has changed (compare line count or checksum)
  * Re-read the playlist file into PLAYLIST_LINES (same logic as playlist_init)
  * Verify current line position still matches expected content
  * If mismatch: scan for the correct line, adjust playlist_line, log warning
  * Recount playlist_total
  * Log if line count changed: "Playlist reloaded: N new lines detected (backup: .ralph/playlist-backup-TIMESTAMP)"
  * If unchanged: no log, no backup (silent no-op)

* In playlist_execute_prompt(), call playlist_reload after invoke_claude returns successfully.
* Do NOT reload after bead execution (beads don't modify the playlist file).

Acceptance criteria:
* If a prompt invocation adds lines after current position, they are picked up on next playlist_next()
* If the file is unchanged, reload is a silent no-op
* Playlist is backed up before reload when changes detected
* Line position is verified by content match, not just line number
* If position mismatch: ralph scans and adjusts (does not skip beads)
* playlist_total is recounted
* Ralph never reads the playlist during a Claude invocation

## Interaction with ralph-0h1.20

playlist_reload() re-reads ACTIONABLE LINES ONLY. The resolved $PLAYLIST_BRANCH is fixed at session start by playlist_resolve_branch() and is NEVER re-resolved from a reloaded header. If a > prompt rewrites the playlist file and changes the leading "# branch: NAME" directive, the new value is ignored at runtime — but log a warning ("playlist reload: # branch: directive changed, ignoring — branch is fixed for the session") so operators see the divergence. Mid-session branch switches would cause commits to land across multiple branches, which is exactly what ralph-0h1.20 exists to prevent.

title: Per-line annotation framework (@turns, @timeout, @model)
description:
Report ref: R7 + R13. Generalizes the existing @model override to a full annotation system.

Support inline metadata on playlist lines: chippie-ogz3.1 @turns=30 @timeout=10 @model=haiku
Parsed by playlist_next(), forwarded to invocation.

Turn/timeout behavior on retry: annotations set the budget for the FIRST attempt only. If the task fails and retries, fall back to global MAX_TURNS/TIMEOUT_MINUTES. The annotation is "try to finish in N turns" — if it can't, the retry gets the full budget to finish the job. This prevents the failure loop where a task that needs 25 turns keeps failing at 20 and exhausts retries.

Implementation:
* In lib/playlist.sh playlist_next(), after classifying bead vs prompt:
  * For bead lines: extract annotations from after the bead ID. Split on whitespace, look for @key=value patterns.
  * For prompt lines: @model is already parsed (without =). Extend to also support @turns=N and @timeout=M. Keep backward compat with >@opus (no =).
  * Set globals: playlist_line_model (existing), playlist_line_turns (new), playlist_line_timeout (new).
  * Default all to empty string (meaning "use global default").
* In lib/playlist.sh playlist_execute_bead() and playlist_execute_prompt():
  * If playlist_line_turns is non-empty, save MAX_TURNS, override, restore after invoke_claude.
  * If playlist_line_timeout is non-empty, save TIMEOUT_MINUTES, override, recalc TIMEOUT_SECS, restore after invoke_claude.
  * On retry (task still in_progress, re-invoked): clear the annotation overrides and use global values. The annotation only applies to the first attempt.
  * playlist_line_model already handled in playlist_execute_prompt(). Extend same pattern to playlist_execute_bead().
* In lib/playlist.sh playlist_dry_run(), display annotations if present:
  log "  1. [bead] chippie-ogz3.1 — Title (@turns=30, @timeout=10)"
* Update the loop counter header (task 7) to show overrides if active.

Acceptance criteria:
* @turns=30 on a bead line sets MAX_TURNS=30 for that invocation only
* @timeout=15 sets TIMEOUT_MINUTES=15 for that invocation only
* @model=opus sets MODEL=opus for that invocation only (beads and prompts)
* All three can be combined: chippie-xxx @turns=30 @timeout=15 @model=sonnet
* On retry: annotation limits are cleared, global values used instead
* Global values are restored after each invocation (whether success or retry)
* Dry-run shows annotations
* Backward compat: >@opus still works (no = sign)

## Interaction with ralph-0h1.20

Branch is deliberately NOT a per-line annotation. ralph-0h1.20 introduces the rule "one branch per playlist", resolved once at startup from CLI > header directive > filename-derived default. The "# branch: NAME" header directive and the "@key=value" per-line annotations are SEPARATE namespaces with different scopes:

* Header directives ("# <key>: <value>" in leading comments, before the first actionable line): session-wide, read once at startup, immutable during the run.
* Per-line annotations ("@key=value" on a bead or prompt line): per-invocation, first-attempt-only, overridable task by task.

Do NOT add @branch=X to the annotation set. A task-scoped branch override would contradict the single-branch invariant and reintroduce exactly the sprawl that ralph-0h1.20 eliminates. If a future need arises to branch mid-playlist, it should be solved by splitting the playlist, not by adding a per-line branch annotation.

title: Quality gate template system
description:
Report ref: §2.11, reworked based on review + external review feedback.

Quality gates are > prompt lines with template tags like #SMOKE_TEST, #COMPLETENESS_SCAN, #REVIEW. Tags are resolved at RUNTIME when ralph builds the prompt for Claude — same mechanism as @opus resolves the model. The playlist file is never modified by expansion.

## Tag Syntax Rules

* One tag per line. Multiple tags on a single line (e.g. > #SMOKE_TEST #REVIEW) is a parse ERROR.
* Unknown tags (not in GATE_TEMPLATES) are a hard ERROR at parse time in playlist_next(). Ralph halts with: "Unknown gate template: #NONEXISTENT on line N. Valid tags: #SMOKE_TEST, #COMPLETENESS_SCAN, #REVIEW"
* Tag-only lines with no user context are valid: > #COMPLETENESS_SCAN expands to just the template base text.
* Tag + user context: >@opus #SMOKE_TEST curl the auth endpoints — template text + user context appended.

## Runtime Expansion (in playlist_execute_prompt)

Playlist line: >@opus #SMOKE_TEST curl every flutter api endpoint against localhost:8080

Ralph parses in playlist_next():
  @opus           → sets playlist_line_model="opus"
  #SMOKE_TEST     → sets playlist_line_gate_tag="SMOKE_TEST"
  "curl every..." → sets playlist_line_gate_context="curl every..."

In playlist_execute_prompt(), before build_raw_prompt():
  If playlist_line_gate_tag is set, call gate_expand_tag(tag, context).
  Returns: template base text + "\n" + user context.
  Pass expanded text to build_raw_prompt(). The #TAG never reaches Claude.

## Implementation

* Create lib/gates.sh with:

  1. GATE_TEMPLATES associative array — base prompt text per tag:
     * SMOKE_TEST: "Test API endpoints against live backend. curl each endpoint implemented in the last batch of beads. Verify responses match expected schemas. If issues found: create beads (type=bug only) with br create, insert IDs into the playlist file after this line."
     * COMPLETENESS_SCAN: "Scan for incomplete work: grep -rn 'TODO|FIXME|HACK|STUB|placeholder|not yet|not implemented' in the project source. For each match in code written during this playlist, implement it fully or remove it with justification. If issues require separate tasks: create beads (type=bug only) and inject into playlist."
     * REVIEW: "Review the work completed in the last epic. Check architecture, patterns, test coverage. Flag issues. If significant work needed: create beads (type=bug only) and inject into playlist."

  2. gate_expand_tag(tag, context): looks up GATE_TEMPLATES[$tag], appends context. Returns combined text.

  3. gate_is_valid_tag(tag): returns 0 if tag exists in GATE_TEMPLATES, 1 otherwise.

  4. gate_check_playlist(): scans PLAYLIST_LINES for #TAG markers. Returns:
     * Total bead count and total gate count
     * Per-template counts
     * Gate density ratio
     * Violations against minimum rules

  5. gate_minimum_rules() — deterministic density requirements:
     * Every playlist with >1 bead MUST have at least 1 gate (zero = ERROR)
     * Density: at least 1 gate per GATE_DENSITY_RATIO beads (default 7, configurable). Low = WARNING.
     * #COMPLETENESS_SCAN: at least once per 10 beads or per epic. Missing = WARNING.
     * #SMOKE_TEST: at least once if playlist has >5 beads. Missing = WARNING.
     * #REVIEW: at least once per epic boundary. Missing = WARNING.

* Config in lib/config.sh:
  * GATE_DENSITY_RATIO=7 (configurable in .ralph/config — starting heuristic, tune after runs)
  * GATE_BUILD_CHECK="" (optional deterministic build command, informational only)
  * GATE_BUILD_EVERY=0 (run build check every N beads, 0 = disabled)

* Runtime parsing in lib/playlist.sh playlist_next():
  * After parsing @model, detect #TAG pattern.
  * Validate tag via gate_is_valid_tag(). If invalid: log error with line number and valid tags, return 1 (halts playlist).
  * If multiple #tags detected on same line: log error, return 1.
  * Store in globals: playlist_line_gate_tag, playlist_line_gate_context.

* In lib/loader.sh, add gates.sh to load order.

Acceptance criteria:
* GATE_TEMPLATES contains SMOKE_TEST, COMPLETENESS_SCAN, REVIEW
* gate_expand_tag() returns template + context at runtime
* Unknown tags are hard errors at parse time with helpful message
* Multiple tags per line are hard errors
* Tag-only lines (no context) expand to template text only
* #TAG is parsed in playlist_next() alongside @model
* Claude never sees raw #TAG — only expanded text
* Playlist file is never modified by expansion
* GATE_DENSITY_RATIO is configurable in .ralph/config
* gate_check_playlist() and gate_minimum_rules() report density analysis

Parse test: create playlist with '>@opus #SMOKE_TEST curl endpoints' — playlist_next should set playlist_line_gate_tag=SMOKE_TEST. Unknown tags halt with error. * Bead ID (e.g., chippie-ogz3.1) — executed as normal bead task

* All existing features (circuit breaker, monitoring, tmux, remote) still work
* Playlist state (current line) persisted in .ralph_state for crash recovery

main loop integration, state tracking/resume, dry-run validation.

title: Parallel playlist execution via git worktrees
description:
Currently two playlists cannot run in parallel in the same repo because
git only supports one branch per working directory. Git worktrees solve
this — each playlist gets its own checkout at a different path, on its
own branch, with no conflict.

High-level design:
* When ralph starts with --playlist, detect the playlist's branch directive
* If a worktree for that branch already exists, reuse it; otherwise create one
  via: git worktree add <path> <branch>
* Run the entire session inside that worktree path
* On session end, optionally remove the worktree or leave it for inspection

Needs further design work:
* Where worktrees are created (sibling dirs? .ralph/worktrees/?)
* How --remote interacts with worktrees
* Cleanup policy (auto-remove vs manual)
* Whether the monitor dashboard needs to aggregate across worktrees
* Race conditions if two sessions target the same branch

Full synthesis at `.ralph/reports/playlist-review-synthesis-2026-04-15.md` (inputs: `.ralph/playlist-review-2026-04-15.md`, `.ralph/reports/chippie-xero-review.md`).

All critical/high findings were verified against the current ralph source tree on 2026-04-15 before this epic was filed. File:line references in each child bead reflect the verified current state.

## Theme

The pattern connecting several findings (C1, C3, P1-commit-leak) is that ralph trusts *symbolic* state (playlist pointer, `playlist-progress.md` claims, Claude's prose close-reasons) over *observable* state (`git status`, `br show`, exit codes). Several fixes below add post-condition checks against observable state.

## Recommended order

1. **C1 + C2 first** (P0 bugs) — both are active footguns: pointer-advance-on-failure orphans beads (orphaned chippie-jy1a.4, skipped #SMOKE_TEST across 3 runs), commit-contradiction lost 6/7 xero test files (untracked while bead closed claiming "47 passing").
2. **C3, H1, H2, H3** (P1) — silent safety erosion, placeholder leak, budget burn.
3. **M1–M5** (P2) — prompt-hygiene sub-batch, can run in parallel.
4. **L1–L3** (P3) — calibration.

## Verification

Each child bead has its own acceptance criteria. Epic-level "done" = all 14 children closed. Smoke test: re-run a short Chippie-style playlist end-to-end (5 beads + 2 gates) and confirm:
* No pointer advance on a forced `exit 1` invocation
* Each bead produces exactly one commit on close (per-bead history preserved)
* Epic auto-closes when all children close (no stuck DONE)
* Non-interactive run aborts without `PLAYLIST_AUTO_CONTINUE=true`

## Children

All children use label `self-improvement` and title prefix `HV:`. Priorities: 3×P0, 4×P1, 5×P2, 3×P3 — but see each bead for the real call.

title: HV: Playlist pointer advances on failed invocation
description:
## Problem

The playlist line pointer advances past a task that failed to execute. Observed across three Chippie xero runs: run-2's `#SMOKE_TEST` invocation hit a usage-limit at turn 1 (exit 1), ralph logged the failure, but `.ralph/state` still advanced `playlist_line` from 6 to 7. Run-3 then started at line 8, skipping both the unfinished `chippie-jy1a.4` (line 6) and the never-executed `#SMOKE_TEST` (line 7). Final `playlist-progress.md` claimed "9/9 items completed" while `br show chippie-jy1a.4` reported `IN_PROGRESS`. Downstream `#REFACTOR` and `#DOCUMENT` gates fired against unverified code.

## Root cause (verified against current source)

`lib/invoke.sh:114-116` increments `total_loops` and calls `save_state` BEFORE invoking Claude:

```
total_loops=\$((total_loops + 1))
save_state
```

`save_state` at `lib/utils.sh:162-163` unconditionally calls `playlist_advance` whenever `PLAYLIST` is set:

```
if [[ -n \"\${PLAYLIST:-}\" && \"\${DRY_RUN:-false}\" != \"true\" ]]; then
    playlist_advance
```

`playlist_advance` at `lib/playlist.sh:115-120` commits `_playlist_pending_line` into `playlist_line`. So the pending line is committed BEFORE Claude's success/failure is known.

`playlist_execute` at `lib/playlist.sh:142,144` tries to reset `_playlist_pending_line=\"\"` on failure, but this is a no-op — the commit to `playlist_line` has already persisted via the pre-invocation `save_state` call.

## Fix (two options, prefer B)

**A. Remove `playlist_advance` from `save_state`** and call it explicitly on the main loop in `ralph` only after `playlist_execute` returns 0. The pre-invocation `save_state` would then only persist loop counters, not pointer progress.

**B. Gate `playlist_advance` inside `save_state` on an explicit flag** (e.g. `_invocation_succeeded`) set only by `playlist_execute` after success; cleared before invocation. Keeps `save_state` a one-call anchor.

Either way: the contract is "playlist_line advances only after a successful playlist_execute".

## Files to modify

* `lib/invoke.sh` (remove the pre-invocation save_state OR keep it but have it skip playlist_advance)
* `lib/utils.sh` (conditionalise playlist_advance in save_state)
* `lib/playlist.sh` (set the success flag after playlist_execute_bead/prompt succeeds)
* `ralph` (main loop may need explicit playlist_advance between playlist_execute and save_state if Option A)

## Acceptance criteria

1. A forced failure (e.g. `--max-turns 1` on a non-trivial bead, or simulated `exit 1`) MUST NOT advance `playlist_line` in `.ralph/state`.
2. The next run of the same playlist picks up at the same line and retries the failed task.
3. Existing success path still advances as before (regression test: 3-bead dry-run playlist still reaches end).
4. `.ralph/state` is still written on failure so `total_loops` and `total_cost_usd` persist.

## Reference

* Synthesis C1: `.ralph/reports/playlist-review-synthesis-2026-04-15.md` lines 39-43
* Report P2 evidence: `.ralph/reports/chippie-xero-review.md` lines 98-116

title: HV: Refactor gate scope cap
description:
## Problem

`templates/gate_refactor.txt` as currently written (lines 14-17) instructs the refactor agent to \"run git diff --stat from the session branch point\" and act on everything it finds. There is no upper bound on the scope. Chippie xero run 3 only stayed focused because the playlist author manually pinned the directory with `#REFACTOR focus on application/services/integrations/xero/`. Without that hand-pin, the gate would have operated on the full `git diff` range — which in run 3 included the entire 02414c7 WIP commit plus all uncommitted work from run 1 (thousands of lines).

## Fix

Add a scope-limit block to `templates/gate_refactor.txt`, preferably right after the Phase 1 Analysis section. Proposed text:

```
## Scope Limit (enforced)
Run \`git diff --stat <session_start_sha>..HEAD\` FIRST, before any analysis.
If the diff touches more than 10 files OR more than 1000 added+deleted lines:
  1. STOP. Do NOT attempt a refactor at this scope.
  2. \`br create --type=bug\` a bead titled \"REFACTOR: scope exceeded — N files / L lines\" with
     the git diff --stat output in its description, and append the ID to the playlist
     via the existing self-healing pattern.
  3. In the new bead's description, ask: \"Which directory should the refactor focus on?\"
  4. Exit this invocation without touching code.
A user-scoped #REFACTOR (e.g. \"#REFACTOR focus on path/to/dir/\") narrows the diff
to that path; apply the 10/1000 check against the narrowed diff.
```

## Files to modify

* `templates/gate_refactor.txt` (pure template change — no shell code)

## Design considerations

* 10 files / 1000 lines are starting thresholds — the playlist author can override by hand-pinning a directory or by raising the threshold in the gate's context annotation (e.g. `> @opus #REFACTOR max_files=20`). Supporting the annotation is out-of-scope for THIS bead; just make the defaults good.
* `<session_start_sha>` — the template currently expects Claude to figure this out via `git log`. Consider exporting `SESSION_START_SHA` as an env variable from `lib/invoke.sh` before spawning Claude. Document the decision in the close reason.
* The `br create` self-healing dance only works when injection is not capped — `strip_injection_instructions` would remove those lines when at the cap (`lib/gates.sh:49-57`). Account for this: the scope-limit block should still halt the refactor even when injection is capped.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A synthetic test playlist with a refactor gate fired over an 11-file diff produces a STOP + bead-creation (with injection enabled) or just a STOP with warning log (with injection capped). No code edits happen.
2. A narrower diff (≤10 files) still refactors as before.
3. `gate_refactor.txt` remains <130 lines (hard template-size guidance from CLAUDE.md §Size Limits).

## Reference

* Synthesis M3: `.ralph/reports/playlist-review-synthesis-2026-04-15.md` lines 85-88
* Chippie xero §4.4: `.ralph/reports/chippie-xero-review.md` lines 210-220

title: HV: Smoke-test gate preconditions
description:
## Problem

`templates/gate_smoke_test.txt` is two lines long:

```
Test API endpoints against live backend. curl each endpoint implemented in the last batch of beads. Verify responses match expected schemas.
If issues found: create beads (type=bug only) with br create, insert IDs into the playlist file after this line.
```

No server-start. No auth/tenant context. No rollback-on-finding. No teardown. This produces false negatives when the dev environment isn't already up, and produces noise beads when auth is the real cause of a 401.

In the Chippie xero retrospective §4.1, this terseness would have resulted in each curl getting a 401 (multi-tenant auth required) and the gate creating noise beads for each 401 before the real checks even began.

## Fix

Rewrite `templates/gate_smoke_test.txt` with explicit preconditions, a closed checklist format, and clean teardown. A concrete rewrite is provided in `.ralph/reports/chippie-xero-review.md` §4.1 (lines 140-154) — adapt but do NOT copy verbatim, because that version is hard-coded to Xero; the template must stay generic.

Proposed generic structure:

```
You are running a smoke test against a live dev environment. This invocation
verifies that endpoints and code paths delivered by the most recent beads
actually work end-to-end.

## Preconditions (run before any checks)

1. Start a dev server in the background (the project's standard command —
   consult README / CLAUDE.md for the project's runner).
2. Wait for the server to respond on its health endpoint.
3. If the project is multi-tenant or requires auth:
   * Look up a seed tenant and/or seed user from the project's test fixtures
     (`tests/helpers/`, `tests/conftest.py`, `tests/fixtures/`).
   * Mint whatever credentials the app needs (session cookie, JWT, API key).
4. If ANY precondition fails: `br create --type=bug` ONE bead titled
   \"SMOKE: preconditions failed — <which step>\", append to playlist, exit.
   Do NOT attempt the checks.

## Checks

Run ALL listed checks; collect failures; report at the end. Do NOT create
beads mid-run — you don't know whether later checks share a root cause with
earlier ones.

For each endpoint added in the session (determine via
\`git diff --name-only <session_start>..HEAD | grep -E 'views|routes|api'\`):
  * curl it with the right method/body/auth
  * assert the documented response (2xx/3xx where applicable, correct
    content-type, key JSON fields present)
  * record pass/fail + evidence

## Output

1 table of {check, passed, evidence-or-error}. If ANY row failed,
\`br create --type=bug\` one bead per distinct root-cause (not one per failing
endpoint; group by root cause) and append IDs to the playlist.

## Teardown

Kill the dev server (PID captured in preconditions). Do not leave background
processes running.

## Rules
* Do NOT fix bugs in this invocation. Detection only.
* If the scenario context below gives specific endpoints/bodies, use them
  verbatim rather than inferring.
* If issues require separate work: create beads (type=bug only) with br create,
  insert IDs into the playlist file after this line.
```

## Files to modify

* `templates/gate_smoke_test.txt` (full rewrite)

## Design considerations

* The gate should stay project-agnostic (it runs across every project that uses ralph). Avoid Chippie-specific terms — keep phrasing like \"the project's standard runner\".
* The scenario-specific context (from `playlist_line_gate_context`) is appended AFTER the template by `gate_expand_tag` at `lib/gates.sh:42-46`. Keep a blank line at the end of the template so the context reads as a separate \"## Scenario\" block naturally.
* Group-by-root-cause bead-creation reduces the risk of flood-creating a bead per 401.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Rewritten `gate_smoke_test.txt` includes explicit preconditions, teardown, and group-by-root-cause bead creation.
2. Template passes the CLAUDE.md \"200-line\" file-size rule.
3. A dry-run smoke test on a small test project produces the expected structure (manual verification noted in close reason).

## Reference

* Synthesis M4: `.ralph/reports/playlist-review-synthesis-2026-04-15.md` lines 90-93
* Chippie xero §4.1 with concrete example: `.ralph/reports/chippie-xero-review.md` lines 126-156

title: HV: Close instruction position in bead prompt
description:
## Problem

The `br close` instruction with `--reason \"VERIFY: [how to test] NOTES: [what changed]\"` boilerplate is the LAST section of the bead prompt (`templates/prompt_bead.txt:29-32`), placed after Orientation, Branch, Rules, File Map, and Playlist Progress. Observed side effect in Chippie xero run 3: bead `.6`'s close reason retained the boilerplate verbatim (`\"VERIFY: [how to test] NOTES: [what changed]\"`) in places instead of fully substituting it — consistent with instruction-fatigue when the close imperative appears 100+ lines after \"Your Task\".

## Fix

Reorder `templates/prompt_bead.txt` so the close instruction is adjacent to \"Your Task\" and the close reason template is presented as a positive instruction with sharp delimiters.

Current order (lines 1-34):
```
1. \"You are executing a single task…\"
3. ## Your Task / ID / Details / Prior Task / Playlist Progress
8. ## Orientation (11 lines)
17. ## Branch
20. ## Rules (numbered)
28. ## File Map
29. ## When Done (close instruction)
```

Proposed order:
```
1. \"You are executing a single task…\"
2. ## Your Task
   ID: {{TASK_ID}}
   On success: br close {{TASK_ID}} --reason \"VERIFY: <exact test command>  NOTES: <≤3 lines on what changed>\"
   On blocked:  br update {{TASK_ID}} --status open  AND write a handoff note in the reason.

   {{DETAILS}}
   {{PRIOR_TASK_CONTEXT}}
   {{PLAYLIST_PROGRESS}}
3. ## Orientation
4. ## Branch
5. ## Rules
6. ## File Map
```

Replace the \"## When Done\" section with a one-line cross-reference if anything remains there, or remove it entirely since it's now in Your Task.

## Files to modify

* `templates/prompt_bead.txt` (reorder — pure template change)

## Acceptance criteria

1. `br close <id> --reason \"…\"` appears within the first 20 lines of the rendered prompt for a bead (manual check on a small test playlist).
2. No content is lost: orientation, branch, rules, file map, and playlist progress all still render (rendered output line-count may change by ±5).
3. Regression: a dry-run bead invocation still produces a well-formed prompt — not a structural break.

## Reference

* Chippie xero §4.3: `.ralph/reports/chippie-xero-review.md` lines 192-208

title: HV: Gate default model + turn cap calibration
description:
## Problem

Two calibration findings bundled (both L-tier but same blast radius and same file set):

**L1 — Gates default to `@opus`, inflating cost.** `lib/gates_inject.sh:84,127` hardcodes `>@opus #SMOKE_TEST` and `>@opus #<TAIL>` when auto-injecting gates. Chippie xero's `#DOCUMENT` ran at opus (30 turns, \$1.35) would have been ~\$0.30 on sonnet. Gates are not a priori harder than bead work — escalate on retry rather than pinning at authoring time.

**L2 — `MAX_TURNS=500` is 7.7× over-provisioned.** `lib/config.sh:16` default. Observed peaks across both retrospectives: 65 (xero), 75 (recurring-jobs). A turn cap of ~100 would still accommodate the P99 bead with room to spare. When a bead genuinely needs more, it can be overridden per-line via `@turns=N`.

## Fix

### L1

In `lib/gates_inject.sh`:

* Remove `@opus` from the hardcoded injected lines — emit `> #SMOKE_TEST`, `> #<TAIL>` instead. The `@opus` annotation stays as a user-opt-in for gate lines where the author explicitly wants opus.

In templates: no change needed — no template text pins `@opus`.

Consider: add a `GATE_DEFAULT_MODEL=sonnet` config var (in `lib/config.sh`) for projects that want to override, but that's optional (keep the change minimal).

### L2

In `lib/config.sh:16`: change `MAX_TURNS=500` to `MAX_TURNS=100`.

Verify `lib/invoke.sh:135` passes `--max-turns \"\$MAX_TURNS\"` so the setting actually propagates (already verified: yes).

Verify `lib/playlist_annotations.sh` respects `@turns=N` overrides so a bead that needs more can still get it.

Update CLAUDE.md's \"Main Loop\" doc section to reflect the new default.

## Files to modify

* `lib/gates_inject.sh` (remove `@opus` from lines 84 and 127)
* `lib/config.sh:16` (change 500 → 100)
* `CLAUDE.md` (update the `--max-turns` doc in the CLI flags section)

## Acceptance criteria

1. Running `ralph playlist init` on a fresh playlist injects gates without `@opus` prefixes (verify: `grep '@opus' <generated-playlist>` is empty unless user hand-added).
2. Default `MAX_TURNS` is 100; `@turns=300` on a single bead in the playlist still applies the override for that bead.
3. CLAUDE.md reflects the new default.
4. No regression: existing playlists with `@opus` manually authored on gate lines still respect that annotation (gates stay on opus when explicitly pinned).

## Reference

* Synthesis L1+L2: `.ralph/reports/playlist-review-synthesis-2026-04-15.md` lines 102-103

title: HV: Retry context accumulation across attempts
description:
## Problem

When `invoke_claude` retries a failed invocation up to `MAX_RETRIES=3` times (`lib/invoke.sh:57-77`), each attempt's retry context block contains `LAST_OUTPUT` from the most recent stream log. The synthesis reports that during Chippie xero run 1, attempts 2 and 3 showed **identical** \"Last output: You've hit your limit\" content — meaning the history doesn't accumulate; the newer attempt overwrites the context of the previous one in the model's view.

Consequence: Claude on attempt 3 cannot see that attempts 1 and 2 both hit the same exit code, so it cannot adapt its strategy (e.g. \"this keeps hitting the same quota — try something structurally different\").

## Root cause (verified)

`lib/invoke_retry.sh::augment_prompt_with_failure_context` (lines 12-28) appends a rendered `retry_context.txt` block to `\$prompt`:

```
retry_block=\$(render_template \"\$TEMPLATES_DIR/retry_context.txt\" …)
prompt=\"\${prompt}\${retry_block}\"
```

It DOES append rather than replace — so the prompt on attempt 3 does include attempt-2's and attempt-3's retry blocks. BUT, each retry block's `LAST_OUTPUT` is re-extracted from the same `INVOKE_LOG` file via `extract_failure_tail` (lines 30-52). For a usage-limit failure, the log tail is identical across attempts — so both retry blocks contain the same \"hit your limit\" text, making them look identical even though they ARE both present.

The fix is not to accumulate (it already does) — it's to **distinguish** each retry block with attempt-specific info: which attempt number, what exit code, and ideally a per-attempt snapshot of diagnosis that differentiates successive attempts.

## Investigation to confirm

Before fixing: open a past session's prompt log (e.g. from `.ralph/logs/sessions/Chippie-xero-integration.playlist-20260415-023942.log`) and search for \"RETRY CONTEXT\" to see what Claude actually saw on attempts 2 and 3. Confirm the hypothesis that the blocks ARE present but visually identical.

## Fix

Update `templates/retry_context.txt` (read it first — path is `\$TEMPLATES_DIR/retry_context.txt`) so each block is clearly scoped as \"Attempt N failed with <diagnosis>\", and add a differentiator that survives identical log tails — e.g. the invocation stream log path and a timestamp.

Optional enhancement (larger scope): maintain a cumulative `retry_history` array in memory across `invoke_claude`'s loop and inject a compact summary (\"Attempt 1: exit 1 (limit). Attempt 2: exit 1 (limit).\") once, rather than appending full blocks. This is more readable for Claude and lower-token.

## Files to modify

* `templates/retry_context.txt` (add per-attempt scoping — read first)
* `lib/invoke_retry.sh` (add timestamp/log-path substitution)
* Optional: `lib/invoke.sh` (maintain retry_history across the loop)

## Acceptance criteria

1. On a manually-triggered 3-failure retry sequence (e.g. via a mocked exit-1 invocation), the rendered prompt on attempt 3 clearly distinguishes the three blocks with attempt numbers and timestamps.
2. When the failure mode is identical across attempts (usage-limit), Claude can still see from the retry context that this is the 3rd instance of the same failure, not the 1st.
3. Regression: a successful first-attempt invocation does not include any retry context block.

## Reference

* Synthesis L3: `.ralph/reports/playlist-review-synthesis-2026-04-15.md` line 104
* Chippie xero evidence: `.ralph/reports/chippie-xero-review.md` table line 238 (\"Retry context lacks cumulative failure history — Confirmed\") and review.md §3.4 reference

title: HV: Branch template contradicts AUTO_COMMIT=false rule
description:
## Problem

In playlist mode (default `AUTO_COMMIT=false`), the rendered bead prompt contains two directly contradictory commit instructions:

* `templates/branch_playlist.txt:3` — \"Commit directly on \`{{BRANCH}}\`. Merging is a separate manual step.\"
* `lib/prompt.sh:136` — \"4. Do NOT commit. Leave changes staged or unstaged — commits are handled externally.\"

Claude consistently obeys Rule 4 (primacy of numbered-list imperative), leaving per-bead work uncommitted. Two documented incidents:

1. **Chippie recurring-jobs run**: 9 beads closed with zero new code commits; Loop 12's `#REFACTOR` gate then swept 2,723 lines of implementation into a single commit labelled \"refactor(recurring-jobs): DRY form parsing, SQL aggregation, dead code cleanup\" (commit `fb63691`). `git log --diff-filter=A` shows `application/services/recurring_job_service.py` (877 lines) appeared in that one commit — it was meant to appear in 9.

2. **Chippie xero run**: bead `chippie-jy1a.6` closed with \"VERIFY: pytest tests/test_xero/ -v — expect 47 passed\" while 6 of 7 test files were *untracked in git*. Closed bead + missing artifacts = the \"no-op pass\" failure mode.

## Root cause (verified)

The branch template is static — it was written assuming commits happen per-bead. `format_commit_rule` at `lib/prompt.sh:132-138` dispatches on AUTO_COMMIT, but the branch template doesn't. Both strings land in the same prompt.

## Fix

### Step 1 — rewrite `templates/branch_playlist.txt` to remove the contradiction

```
You are working on branch \`{{BRANCH}}\`. This is the single branch for this entire playlist session.
Do NOT create feature branches. Do NOT run \`git checkout\` to any other branch.
Commits on \`{{BRANCH}}\` are made by the outer loop after \`br close\`.
Do NOT run \`git add\`, \`git commit\`, or \`git stash\` — if you commit yourself,
the per-bead history is lost and downstream gates cannot attribute work to beads.
```

### Step 2 — decision point: who commits?

The branch template above asserts \"outer loop commits after br close\". For this to be true, ONE of these must also be true:

* **Option A**: Flip `AUTO_COMMIT=true` as the default for playlist mode (the inner loop commits). Current default `AUTO_COMMIT=true` in `lib/config.sh:29` is already this — but the comment at `lib/config.sh:27-28` says \"In playlist mode, defaults to false\". Check whether any playlist entry point forces it to false; align reality to docs.
* **Option B**: Keep `AUTO_COMMIT=false` but add outer-loop per-bead commit in `lib/task_outcome.sh` after `br close`. Filed as its own bead (`HV: Outer loop auto-commits per-bead after br close`) because it's ~15 lines of new functionality.

**This bead's scope is Step 1 + the decision**; Step 2-B implementation lives in the sibling chore bead. Pick A or B and document rationale on this bead before closing.

## Files to modify

* `templates/branch_playlist.txt` (rewrite)
* `lib/config.sh` (if option A: update comment at lines 27-28 and/or explicit playlist-mode default)
* Possibly `lib/playlist.sh` or `lib/lifecycle.sh` (if playlist mode explicitly overrides AUTO_COMMIT elsewhere — search for `AUTO_COMMIT` before assuming)

## Acceptance criteria

1. Rendered playlist-mode prompt contains no internally-contradictory commit instructions (verify by grepping the test prompt for both \"Commit directly\" and \"Do NOT commit\" — at most one should match).
2. The chosen option (A or B) is recorded in this bead's close `--reason` so harvesters can see the decision.
3. On a test playlist run, per-bead commits appear in `git log` (one per closed bead) OR the decision is explicitly B and the sibling chore is wired to produce them.

## Reference

* Synthesis C2: `.ralph/reports/playlist-review-synthesis-2026-04-15.md` lines 45-49
* Chippie recurring-jobs evidence: `.ralph/playlist-review-2026-04-15.md` \"3 things that went poorly\" #1
* Chippie xero evidence: `.ralph/reports/chippie-xero-review.md` P1 (lines 64-96)

title: HV: Outer loop auto-commits per-bead after br close
description:
## Context

Sibling of `HV: Branch template contradicts AUTO_COMMIT=false rule`. That bead rewrites the branch template to say \"the outer loop commits after br close\" and forces a decision:

* **A**: flip `AUTO_COMMIT=true` as playlist-mode default (inner loop commits).
* **B**: keep `AUTO_COMMIT=false`, have the outer loop commit after each `br close`.

**This bead implements Option B only.** Do NOT start it until the sibling bead closes with option B chosen. If option A was chosen, close this bead as wontfix with a reference to the sibling's decision rationale.

## Problem (repeated for standalone context)

In playlist mode with `AUTO_COMMIT=false`, no process commits per-bead work. Downstream gates (`#REFACTOR`, `#DOCUMENT`) sweep accumulated changes into a single commit, destroying per-bead history. 2,723 lines collapsed into one mislabelled commit in the Chippie recurring-jobs retrospective.

## Implementation plan

Add per-bead commit to `lib/task_outcome.sh::handle_task_outcome` in the `closed)` arm (currently at `lib/task_outcome.sh:15-24`), AFTER `br close` has been recorded by Claude and `check_bead_status` confirmed `closed`.

Sketch:

```
closed)
    total_tasks_completed=\$((total_tasks_completed + 1))
    log \"Task …\"
    capture_task_handoff \"\$tid\"
    mark_needs_review \"\$tid\"
    commit_bead_work \"\$tid\"    # <-- NEW
    maybe_close_epic \"\$tid\"
    current_task=\"\"
    ;;
```

Where `commit_bead_work` (new helper, same file):

```
commit_bead_work() {
    local tid=\"\$1\"
    [[ \"\$AUTO_COMMIT\" == \"true\" ]] && return  # inner loop already committed
    git diff --quiet && git diff --cached --quiet && return  # nothing to commit
    local title slug
    title=\$(get_bead_field \"\$tid\" title)
    slug=\$(slugify \"\$title\")
    git add -A
    git commit --no-verify -m \"feat(\${slug}): close \${tid}

\${title}

Closes \${tid}.\"
}
```

`get_bead_field` exists at `lib/utils_beads.sh:18`. `slugify` exists in `lib/tasks.sh` (verify name; search before importing).

## Files to modify

* `lib/task_outcome.sh` (add `commit_bead_work` helper + call site in `handle_task_outcome`)
* Possibly `lib/tasks.sh` if `slugify` needs exporting

## Design considerations

* **Do NOT** `git add -A` if sandbox mode changes the root — scope to `git add -A .` from the project root.
* The `.beads/` sync commit done by `commit_beads_if_dirty` runs BEFORE invocation; by the time `br close` lands, there may be a new `.beads/issues.jsonl` change from the close itself. Include it in the per-bead commit (clean working tree after close) or call `commit_beads_if_dirty` after `commit_bead_work` — pick one and stay consistent with existing flow.
* `--no-verify` is already the ralph convention (see `commit_beads_if_dirty` at `lib/utils.sh:104`).
* If the working tree is already clean at close time (nothing Claude did modified files — e.g. the bead was a docs-only research bead), skip the commit — a guard like `git diff --quiet && git diff --cached --quiet && return` handles it.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Running a 3-bead playlist in playlist mode with `AUTO_COMMIT=false` produces 3 new commits on the playlist branch (one per bead, excluding `chore(ralph): sync beads state` commits).
2. Each per-bead commit's message references the bead ID (`Closes ralph-…`) and carries the bead title in its subject or body.
3. A bead that closes without modifying any code does NOT produce an empty commit.
4. Subsequent `#REFACTOR` gate sees only refactor-specific diffs in its `git diff` window, not prior bead implementations.

title: HV: Epic auto-close fails when child in DONE state
description:
## Problem

Chippie recurring-jobs retrospective: epic `chippie-9zsi` stayed `open` after all 9 children completed. Child `chippie-9zsi.7` was stuck in status `DONE` (not `closed`). No `verified:needs-review` label was applied to `.7`, unlike its siblings. `ralph` never auto-closed the epic.

## Root cause (verified)

`lib/task_outcome.sh:110-126::maybe_close_epic` uses `count_open_epic_children` which is defined at `lib/utils_beads.sh:35-38`:

```
count_open_epic_children() {
    br show \"\$1\" --json 2>/dev/null \\
        | jq '[.[0].dependents // [] | .[] | select(.dependency_type == \"parent-child\") | select(.status != \"closed\")] | length' 2>/dev/null
}
```

The filter is `select(.status != \"closed\")`. A child in status `DONE` satisfies that filter (DONE != closed), so the count is nonzero and the epic auto-close is skipped. `DONE` is evidently a transient bead state that can slip through when `br update --claim` and `br close` race.

## Fix (two-part)

**Part A — treat DONE as closed-equivalent in the children count:**

In `lib/utils_beads.sh::count_open_epic_children`, change the jq selector to:

```
select(.status != \"closed\" and .status != \"DONE\" and .status != \"done\")
```

Or (cleaner) positively match only open/in_progress states:

```
select(.status == \"open\" or .status == \"in_progress\" or .status == \"blocked\" or .status == \"ready\")
```

Pick whichever matches the beads_rust status vocabulary — check with `br list --status=<status>` whether the DONE case-sensitivity is `DONE` or `done`.

**Part B — roll DONE forward to CLOSED after close:**

In `lib/task_outcome.sh::handle_task_outcome`, the `closed)` arm trusts `bead_status==\"closed\"`. Add a defensive roll-forward for `DONE`: if `check_bead_status` returns `DONE` or the post-close re-check returns `DONE`, call `br close <id>` explicitly with a reason like \"Auto-rolled forward from DONE\". Also apply `mark_needs_review` which currently only runs in the `closed` arm.

Consider extending `check_bead_status` at `lib/invoke.sh:176-189` to case-fold `DONE`→`closed` at the source.

## Files to modify

* `lib/utils_beads.sh::count_open_epic_children` (Part A)
* `lib/task_outcome.sh` and/or `lib/invoke.sh::check_bead_status` (Part B)

## Open questions for implementer

* Is `DONE` a legitimate beads_rust state or is it the display string from `br show --json`? Run `br show <known-closed-bead> --json | jq '.[0].status'` on a few historical beads to find out.
* If `DONE` is a transient produced only by `br close --suggest-next`, consider reporting upstream to beads_rust as a separate chore.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Given an epic with all children at various mixes of `closed` and `DONE`, `maybe_close_epic` closes the epic.
2. `chippie-9zsi.7` or a fixture equivalent: after ralph processes it, it ends in `closed` (not `DONE`) and carries the `verified:needs-review` label.
3. Regression: a genuinely-open child still blocks epic close.

## Reference

* Synthesis C3: `.ralph/reports/playlist-review-synthesis-2026-04-15.md` lines 51-54
* Chippie recurring-jobs unpredicted findings #2 and #3: `.ralph/playlist-review-2026-04-15.md` lines 193-196

title: HV: Non-interactive validation prompt silent-proceeds
description:
## Problem

When a playlist is missing the `✓ VALIDATED:` marker (i.e. was never through `ralph playlist init`), a warning is logged and the session continues silently under non-interactive execution. All three Chippie xero runs bypassed the semantic audit this way.

## Root cause (verified)

`lib/playlist_marker.sh:38-42`:

```
prompt_for_validation() {
    if [[ ! -t 0 ]]; then
        log \"WARNING: Playlist not validated (non-interactive, continuing)\"
        return
    fi
    …
}
```

Non-interactive (no TTY on stdin) immediately returns after logging — the session proceeds. This is the opposite of a fail-safe default: the common case (tmux, CI, `ralph --remote`, detached agent runs) silently skips the validation gate that was designed to enforce semantic review.

## Fix

Change the non-interactive branch to HALT unless explicitly opted out via config or CLI. Proposed behaviour:

```
prompt_for_validation() {
    if [[ ! -t 0 ]]; then
        if [[ \"\${PLAYLIST_AUTO_CONTINUE:-false}\" == \"true\" || \"\${YES:-false}\" == \"true\" ]]; then
            log \"WARNING: Playlist not validated (non-interactive, PLAYLIST_AUTO_CONTINUE=true)\"
            return
        fi
        log \"ERROR: Playlist not validated and running non-interactively.\"
        log \"  Run \\\"ralph playlist init \$PLAYLIST\\\" first, or set PLAYLIST_AUTO_CONTINUE=true in .ralph/config, or pass --yes.\"
        exit 1
    fi
    …
}
```

## Files to modify

* `lib/playlist_marker.sh` (the non-interactive branch)
* `lib/args.sh` (add `--yes` flag if not already present — search for `--yes` before adding)
* `lib/config.sh` (`PLAYLIST_AUTO_CONTINUE=false` default; document the variable)

## Acceptance criteria

1. `ralph --playlist unvalidated.playlist < /dev/null` (non-interactive stdin) exits 1 with the error message. Previously it silent-proceeded.
2. `PLAYLIST_AUTO_CONTINUE=true ralph --playlist unvalidated.playlist < /dev/null` proceeds with a warning (preserves the escape hatch for CI).
3. `ralph --yes --playlist unvalidated.playlist < /dev/null` proceeds with a warning.
4. Interactive run (`-t 0` true) still prompts `[y/N]` as before.
5. Updating CLAUDE.md or GUIDE.md to document `PLAYLIST_AUTO_CONTINUE` is part of this bead's scope.

## Reference

* Chippie xero evidence: `.ralph/reports/chippie-xero-review.md` U2 (lines 257-262)

title: HV: Placeholder leak in rendered gates — & mangled to {{PROMPT_TEXT}}
description:
## Problem

Session log for Chippie recurring-jobs run showed the rendered `#DOCUMENT` prompt contained:

```
│ - **Edge Cases {{PROMPT_TEXT}} Limitations**: known limitations, assumptions
```

The template source at `templates/gate_document.txt:73` reads `**Edge Cases & Limitations**`. The literal `&` was replaced with the *key* of a pending substitution (`{{PROMPT_TEXT}}`). This is the signature of sed-style substitution where `&` is a back-reference for the match; an unescaped `&` in the replacement value fed to `sed 's/…/…/'` expands to the matched pattern.

Claude ignored the garbled heading and produced sensible docs, but this is a live prompt-hygiene bug that could corrupt more load-bearing text in future.

## Investigation needed (verification surprise)

`lib/utils.sh:180-190::render_template` uses pure-bash parameter expansion:

```
content=\"\${content//\\{\\{\$key\\}\\}/\$value}\"
```

Bash's `${var//pat/repl}` does NOT treat `&` as a back-reference — so `render_template` itself cannot produce this corruption. The mangling must happen somewhere else in the chain from playlist → `gate_expand_tag` → `build_raw_prompt` → rendered output → display.

**Likely suspects to audit first:**

* `lib/gates.sh::gate_expand_tag` (lines 33-47) — uses `printf '%s\\n%s'` concatenation; safe.
* `lib/gates.sh::strip_injection_instructions` (lines 55-57) — uses `grep -v`; safe.
* `lib/utils.sh::show_prompt` (lines 54-76) — uses `printf` with `%s`; safe.
* `lib/format_stream.sh` — display pipeline, possibly uses `sed`.
* `prompt_raw.txt` or `prompt_bead.txt` rendering — if `PROMPT_TEXT` value contains `&` that value gets substituted FIRST into the rendered prompt, then when Claude's stream-json echoes it back into `format_stream` there may be a sed pass there.

**Most likely culprit:** the `show_prompt`/display pipeline's interaction with `format_stream.sh` — specifically any `sed` filter that re-rewrites the prompt text. Check `lib/format_stream.sh` (not yet inspected) and any `sed 's/.../.../'` in display helpers.

## Fix

1. Find the sed (or printf `%b`) call that treats `&` as a back-reference.
2. Either escape `&` in replacement strings (`sed 's/…/\\\&…/'`) or migrate the call to pure-bash parameter expansion or to `awk` which doesn't have the back-reference quirk.
3. Add a regression fixture: a gate template containing `&`, `\\0`, `\\1` in both the base text and the injected context, rendered end-to-end, asserting the literal characters survive to the `show_prompt` output.

## Files to modify

* Likely `lib/format_stream.sh` (confirm via grep for `sed` across `lib/`)
* Possibly any other display helper that chains a `sed` call
* Add a test (bash harness under `tests/` if one exists; otherwise document the manual repro in the bead close reason)

## Acceptance criteria

1. Root cause identified and named in the close reason (\"the `&` → `{{PROMPT_TEXT}}` leak was caused by X in file:line\").
2. Regression case: a playlist line like `> #DOCUMENT foo & bar` renders in the session log with the literal `&` preserved.
3. `grep -rn \"sed 's/\" lib/ templates/` reviewed — any remaining `sed` substitutions either have escaped `&` in replacements or are documented as safe.

## Reference

* Synthesis H2: `.ralph/reports/playlist-review-synthesis-2026-04-15.md` lines 63-66
* Chippie recurring-jobs Finding E: `.ralph/playlist-review-2026-04-15.md` lines 164-165

title: HV: Completion report retries on usage-limit
description:
## Problem

In Chippie xero run 1, the final 5 invocations were all the completion-report prompt (generated by `lib/lifecycle.sh::generate_playlist_report`) re-running against an already-exhausted usage window. Each attempt returned exit 1 from the usage-limit; `invoke_claude`'s 3-retry loop fired for each, burning budget on non-load-bearing telemetry.

## Root cause (verified)

`lib/lifecycle.sh:132-136`:

```
build_report_prompt \"\$report_dir\" \"\$report_file\" \"\$playlist_data\" \"\$git_log\"
invoke_claude || {
    log \"WARNING: Report generation failed. Continuing cleanup.\"
    return
}
```

The `invoke_claude || …` already handles the final failure — but `invoke_claude` internally retries up to `MAX_RETRIES=3` times (`lib/invoke.sh:4,57-77`) before giving up. For a usage-limit exit, those retries are futile: the limit is a time-window condition the retry cannot fix within the retry window.

Additionally, `wait_for_quota` (called at `lib/invoke.sh:69`) may sleep for the reset window — meaning a failed report can sleep the session for 5 hours before giving up. That is emphatically worse than skipping the report.

## Fix

The completion report is non-load-bearing. It should either:

* **Option A** (recommended): add a param to `invoke_claude` (or a sibling `invoke_claude_once`) that skips retry and quota-wait, and use it from `generate_playlist_report`.
* **Option B**: inside `generate_playlist_report`, check a specific exit code (usage-limit) before calling `invoke_claude` or intercept the first exit and skip remaining retries.

Option A is cleaner: the callsite expresses intent (\"fire-and-forget\"), no exit-code sniffing required. Sketch:

```
# In invoke.sh:
invoke_claude_no_retry() {
    MAX_RETRIES=1 invoke_claude
}

# In lifecycle.sh:
invoke_claude_no_retry || {
    log \"WARNING: Report generation failed. Continuing cleanup.\"
    return
}
```

(Note: `MAX_RETRIES=1` means one attempt total, no retries. Confirm by reading `invoke_claude` loop condition `[[ \$attempt -le \$MAX_RETRIES ]]` — the loop body runs once, and the first failure hits `[[ \$attempt -ge \$MAX_RETRIES ]]` so it returns immediately.)

Also ensure `wait_for_quota` doesn't fire when retries are disabled (either by gating on `MAX_RETRIES > 1` in `invoke_claude`, or by factoring it out).

## Files to modify

* `lib/invoke.sh` (add the fire-and-forget variant; gate wait_for_quota)
* `lib/lifecycle.sh:133` (swap invoke_claude → invoke_claude_no_retry)

## Acceptance criteria

1. When the session hits a usage limit during the completion-report phase, ralph logs the WARNING and exits cleanly within 30 seconds (no retry loop, no 5-hour sleep).
2. Regression: a successful completion-report invocation still writes the report file as before.
3. Inner-loop invocations (beads, gates) retain their 3-retry + quota-wait behaviour.

## Reference

* Synthesis H3: `.ralph/reports/playlist-review-synthesis-2026-04-15.md` lines 68-71
* Chippie xero U3: `.ralph/reports/chippie-xero-review.md` lines 264-265

title: HV: Epic description spec-file extraction convention
description:
## Problem

Report 2 §4.2 measured ~720 redundant lines of epic-scoped context duplicated across 9 invocations in the Chippie xero run (~32k recomputed tokens). Sections like \"Pricing (AUD, tax exclusive)\", \"AI/ML Compliance\", \"Existing Code\" were irrelevant to every individual bead yet re-injected every invocation because they lived in the epic `description` which each child prompt inherits.

This is not a ralph bug per se — it's an authoring convention gap. But the cost is real and compounds with every epic.

## Proposed convention

**Epic descriptions should link to a spec file, not inline the spec.**

Current (bad):
```
## Scope
* OAuth 2.0 with PKCE …
* ONE-WAY contact sync …
…80 lines of spec prose…
```

New (good):
```
Xero accounting integration for Chippie tenants (AU/GB/IE).
Specification: docs/technical/features/XERO_SPEC.md
Branch: xero-integration.playlist — cherry-picked from xero@65021d1 in task .1
```

Per-bead descriptions then carry only the task-specific scope. Claude reads the spec file on demand if needed (directed by the task description), not proactively on every bead.

## Scope of THIS bead

Documentation + tooling to encourage the convention, NOT a refactor of existing epics. Concrete deliverables:

1. Add a short section to `CLAUDE.md` (or `GUIDE.md` — pick whichever the project already uses for authoring conventions) titled \"Epic description conventions\" covering:
   * \"Link, don't inline\" rule
   * Where spec files should live (suggest `docs/technical/features/<epic-slug>_SPEC.md` or project-local equivalent)
   * What the epic description SHOULD contain (3–5 line summary + path link + branch/provenance notes)
   * What the bead description SHOULD contain (task-specific scope only)
2. Add a lint/advisory check in `ralph playlist init`'s semantic audit phase that warns when an epic description exceeds N lines (suggest N=40) OR when the same ≥20-line block appears verbatim across multiple children.
3. Optionally update `lib/playlist_semantic.sh` prompt to encourage the reviewer to flag this pattern.

## Files to modify

* `CLAUDE.md` or `GUIDE.md` (authoring-conventions section)
* `lib/playlist_semantic.sh` (add to the semantic-audit prompt — read the file first; do not invent sections it doesn't have)
* Possibly `lib/playlist_validate.sh` (pure-bash line-count warning)

## Non-scope

* Do NOT rewrite historical Chippie epics as part of this bead.
* Do NOT try to auto-extract spec prose from existing epics (would require judgment calls per-epic).

## Acceptance criteria

1. The convention is documented with an example (good vs bad).
2. A future playlist run whose epic has a ≥40-line description produces an advisory warning in playlist-init semantic audit.
3. Closing this bead references the exact doc section path (e.g. \"CLAUDE.md §Epic description conventions\").

## Reference

* Synthesis M1: `.ralph/reports/playlist-review-synthesis-2026-04-15.md` lines 75-78
* Chippie xero evidence: `.ralph/reports/chippie-xero-review.md` §4.2 (lines 158-189)

title: HV: Playlist progress block noise on early beads
description:
## Problem

The `## Playlist Progress` block injected into every prompt (via `lib/playlist_progress.sh::format_playlist_progress`) emits the full \"Remaining\" list of not-yet-started items on every invocation. On the first bead of a 13-item playlist, that's ~16 lines of noise about tasks the current agent cannot act on. Report 1 Finding D measured ~150–300 tokens × N invocations of avoidable bloat.

## Root cause (verified)

`lib/playlist_progress.sh::playlist_write_progress` (lines 11-71) iterates every actionable line in the playlist and categorises it as `completed_items`, `in_progress_line`, or `remaining_items`. The rendered file always includes the full `## Remaining` block, and `format_playlist_progress` (lines 104-108) simply `cat`s the file into the prompt.

There is no truncation or lookahead cap.

## Fix

Modify `playlist_write_progress` (preferred — smaller and keeps `format_playlist_progress` pure) to:

* When `completed` is 0 (we're on the first actionable line), emit only:
  ```
  Position: 1/N · Next: <format_progress_item of the +1 item>
  ```
* When `completed >= 1`, emit the `Completed` list, the `In Progress` line, and the `Remaining` list **capped at +3 lookahead** (with a `…plus K more` tail line when truncated).

Preserve the existing file-based writeback so `monitor` and debug tooling still see the full state (the cap applies only to the prompt-facing excerpt, not the full progress file) — OR, alternatively, cap the file too and let monitoring read the playlist directly. Pick one.

**Simpler variant**: cap the Remaining list unconditionally at 3 entries in `format_playlist_progress`, keeping `playlist_write_progress` unchanged. Less code, same token saving for the prompt.

## Files to modify

* `lib/playlist_progress.sh` (`format_playlist_progress` and/or `playlist_write_progress`)

## Acceptance criteria

1. On a 13-bead playlist, the first prompt's `## Playlist Progress` section is ≤ 5 lines.
2. On a mid-run prompt (say bead 7 of 13), the section includes all 6 completed items but only +3 remaining items, with a `…plus N more` indicator when ≥4 remain.
3. Regression: the full progress file at `.ralph/playlist-progress.md` still tracks the entire playlist for the monitor dashboard (OR, if chosen otherwise, the tradeoff is documented in the close reason).

## Reference

* Synthesis M2: `.ralph/reports/playlist-review-synthesis-2026-04-15.md` lines 80-83
* Chippie recurring-jobs Finding D: `.ralph/playlist-review-2026-04-15.md` lines 152-162

title: Task queue and schedule-aware execution
description:
# Task queue and schedule-aware execution

## Context

Ralph currently requires manual invocation for every run. The user wants to queue multiple
ralph invocations ahead of time (playlists, scoped runs, etc.) and have them execute
automatically according to a schedule. The primary driver is Claude Max plan usage
management: runs should happen during off-hours to maximise available tokens for the
user's working day, and should not start if the 5-hour usage bucket is too depleted.
Secondary drivers are the user's hours of operation and weekly usage burn-rate monitoring.

The user runs ralph primarily on a remote Oracle server (opc@oracle) so their local
machine can be powered off. The scheduling system must support remote install so the
scheduler runs on the remote, supervised by the remote OS.

## Architecture: stateless tick + OS timer (no daemon, no wait loop)

Rejected: a long-running foreground wait loop. Unacceptable for overnight/remote use and
not the right process-management idiom on either darwin or linux.

Adopted: **stateless one-shot tick**, invoked periodically by the OS scheduler
(launchd StartInterval on darwin, systemd user .timer on linux). Each tick:

1. Acquires flock on .ralph/schedule.lock (non-blocking; exits 0 if held).
2. Reads .ralph/schedule-config (AT, STOP_AT, USAGE_MIN).
3. Evaluates all conditions against current time + claude-usage state.
4. If conditions met and queue non-empty: pops head entry, runs 'ralph $entry'
   synchronously, removes entry on success.
5. Writes .ralph/schedule-state with status, queue depth, next-tick ETA, last result.
6. Releases lock and exits.

OS timer fires the tick every 5min (configurable). While a ralph entry is running
(may be hours), subsequent ticks fast-exit on the lock — no concurrency hazard, no
PID tracking.

## Top-level concepts

* **Queue** (.ralph/queue) — text file, one ralph-args line per entry. Managed via
  'ralph queue {add|list|next|remove|clear}'. Unchanged from original design.

* **Schedule config** (.ralph/schedule-config) — key=value file holding AT, STOP_AT,
  USAGE_MIN, TICK_INTERVAL. Written by 'ralph schedule install [flags]' or
  'ralph schedule reconfigure'. Read by every tick.

* **Schedule state** (.ralph/schedule-state) — key=value file written by every tick.
  Keys: status (idle|running|waiting), waiting_for (condition string), queue_depth,
  current_entry, last_tick, next_tick_eta, last_run_result. This is the stable
  surface for external observers (tmux statusbar, monitors, humans).

* **Schedule CLI** — 'ralph schedule {install|uninstall|tick|status|logs|attach|reconfigure}'.
  Install generates the OS unit file + loads it. Tick is what the OS calls. Status,
  logs, attach are the observability surface. Attach is specifically for when a tick
  launched a ralph entry in a tmux session — attaches to it.

## Approach

1. Extend /Users/admin/bin/claude-usage with --available N flag (DONE in ralph-yui.1).
2. Add 'ralph queue' subcommand + lib/queue.sh (ralph-yui.2, unchanged).
3. Add lib/schedule.sh: stateless condition evaluators, schedule-config + schedule-state
   I/O, flock helpers (ralph-yui.3, rewritten for tick pattern).
4. Fix build_forward_args for --playlist + sync .ralph/schedule-config to remote
   alongside .ralph/queue (ralph-yui.4).
5. Add 'ralph schedule' subcommand with install/uninstall/tick/status/logs/attach
   surface, plus launchd plist and systemd user unit templates. Remote mode rsyncs
   config + SSHes to run 'ralph schedule install' on the remote. (ralph-yui.5, rewritten.)

## Critical files

* /Users/admin/bin/claude-usage — DONE (ralph-yui.1)
* lib/args.sh — add 'queue' and 'schedule' subcommands with nested verbs
* lib/queue.sh (NEW) — queue file read/write (ralph-yui.2)
* lib/schedule.sh (NEW) — condition evaluators, config/state I/O, tick orchestration
* lib/remote.sh — fix build_forward_args; add sync_schedule_config_to_remote
* lib/config.sh — add QUEUE_FILE, SCHEDULE_CONFIG, SCHEDULE_STATE, SCHEDULE_LOCK paths
* templates/launchd-scheduler.plist — launchd agent template
* templates/systemd-scheduler.service — systemd user service template
* templates/systemd-scheduler.timer — systemd user timer template

## Verification

* ralph queue add --playlist plan.playlist && ralph queue list  # entry appears
* ralph schedule install --usage-available 40 --at 22:00 --stop-at 06:00
  # writes .ralph/schedule-config, generates + loads OS unit
* ralph schedule status  # shows config, state, queue depth, next tick ETA, OS unit status
* ralph schedule tick  # manual one-shot; if all conditions met and queue non-empty,
                       # runs head entry and removes it
* ralph schedule uninstall  # unloads + removes OS unit
* ralph schedule install -r oracle --usage-available 40
  # syncs ralph + queue + schedule-config; SSHes and runs install on oracle
* OS timer fires tick while another tick is running → second tick exits 0 immediately
  (flock held), no duplicate entry execution

title: claude-usage: add --5-hour and --7-day flags for targeted output
description:
## What to implement

Extend /Users/admin/bin/claude-usage with two new flags:

1. --available N  — exit 0 if 5-hour usage has at least N% available (i.e.
   100 - five_hour.used_percent >= N), exit 1 otherwise. This is the scheduling
   primitive used by lib/schedule.sh to decide whether to start a queue run.
   Example: 'claude-usage --available 40' exits 0 when 5h usage is <= 60%.

2. --5-hour  — output only the five_hour JSON block (for targeted scripting).
   Example: claude-usage --5-hour | jq .resets_in_minutes

3. --7-day  — output only the seven_day JSON block (for burn-rate monitoring).
   Example: claude-usage --7-day | jq .used_percent

## File to modify

* /Users/admin/bin/claude-usage  (lines 16-40 for arg parsing, line 110 area for check mode)

## Implementation

In the parse args section (while [[ $# -gt 0 ]] loop, lines 19-40), add:

  --available)
    MODE="available"
    THRESHOLD="${2:?--available requires a threshold percentage}"
    shift 2
    ;;
  --5-hour) MODE="five_hour"; shift ;;
  --7-day)  MODE="seven_day"; shift ;;

In the case "$MODE" block, add:

  available)
    PCT=$(echo "$RESPONSE" | jq '
      if .five_hour then (100 - (.five_hour.utilization // 0 | round))
      else 0 end
    ')
    if (( PCT >= THRESHOLD )); then exit 0; else exit 1; fi
    ;;
  five_hour)
    echo "$RESPONSE" | jq '
      def parse_ts: sub("\\+00:00$"; "Z") | sub("\\.[0-9]+Z$"; "Z") | fromdateiso8601;
      if .five_hour then {
        used_percent: (.five_hour.utilization // 0 | round),
        resets_at: .five_hour.resets_at,
        resets_in_minutes: ((.five_hour.resets_at | parse_ts) - now | . / 60 | round)
      } else null end'
    ;;
  seven_day)
    echo "$RESPONSE" | jq '
      def parse_ts: sub("\\+00:00$"; "Z") | sub("\\.[0-9]+Z$"; "Z") | fromdateiso8601;
      if .seven_day then {
        used_percent: (.seven_day.utilization // 0 | round),
        resets_at: .seven_day.resets_at,
        resets_in_minutes: ((.seven_day.resets_at | parse_ts) - now | . / 60 | round)
      } else null end'
    ;;

Also update the --help output and usage string (lines 28-36) to document the three new flags.

Note on no-data case: claude-usage returns no data when no Claude session has run recently.
The --available flag should treat no-data as "not available" (exit 1) so the schedule loop
does not start blindly. Add a guard: if five_hour is null, exit 1.

## Acceptance criteria

* claude-usage --available 40  exits 0 when 5h used_percent <= 60%, exits 1 when > 60%
* claude-usage --available 99  exits 1 (5h is never 99% free in practice)
* claude-usage --5-hour        outputs JSON with used_percent, resets_at, resets_in_minutes
* claude-usage --7-day         outputs JSON with used_percent, resets_at, resets_in_minutes
* claude-usage --help          documents all three new flags
* No-data case (no active sessions): --available exits 1, --5-hour outputs null

All acceptance criteria verified: --available exits 0/1 based on available percentage, --5-hour and --7-day output targeted JSON blocks with used_percent, resets_at, resets_in_minutes, --help documents all new flags, no-data case handled (exits 1 for --available, outputs null for time window modes).

title: Implement queue file format and queue subcommand
description:
## What to implement

Create lib/queue.sh with queue file management functions, and add 'ralph queue' subcommand
to lib/args.sh and dispatch in dispatch_early_exit_action.

Queue file: .ralph/queue (one ralph-args line per entry, e.g. '--playlist plan.playlist').
Comments (#) and blank lines are skipped by the reader. Completed entries are deleted from
the file (not commented) so the file always shows pending work.

## Files to create/modify

* lib/queue.sh (NEW) — queue operations
* lib/args.sh  — add 'queue' to parse_arg_flags and dispatch_early_exit_action
* lib/loader.sh — add 'source "$LIB_DIR/queue.sh"' after config.sh
* lib/config.sh — add QUEUE_FILE=".ralph/queue" default
* templates/usage.txt — document ralph queue subcommand

## lib/queue.sh functions

queue_file() — returns path to queue file (from $QUEUE_FILE global)

queue_read_entries() — prints non-blank, non-comment lines from queue file, one per line

queue_count() — count of pending entries

queue_add() — appends args string as new line to queue file; creates file if missing
  Usage: queue_add "--playlist plan.playlist"

queue_list() — numbered display of queue entries (log "  1. --playlist plan.playlist")

queue_next() — prints the first non-blank non-comment line without modifying the file

queue_remove_first() — removes the first non-blank non-comment line from the queue file;
  used by schedule.sh after each entry completes

queue_remove_nth() — removes line N (1-based, counting only non-comment non-blank lines)

queue_clear() — truncates .ralph/queue to empty

## args.sh changes

In parse_arg_flags, after the 'playlist' case, add:

  queue)
    case "${2:-}" in
      add)
        ACTION="queue_add"

        return

      next)  ACTION="queue_next";   shift 2 ;;

      remove)
        ACTION="queue_remove"
        QUEUE_REMOVE_N="${3:?ralph queue remove requires a position number}"
        shift 3
        ;;
      *)
        log "ERROR: Usage: ralph queue {add|list|next|clear|remove N}"
        exit 1
        ;;
    esac
    ;;

In dispatch_early_exit_action, add cases before the MONITOR_MODE check:

  queue_add)    queue_add "$QUEUE_ADD_ARGS"; queue_list; exit 0 ;;
  queue_list)   queue_list; exit 0 ;;

  queue_clear)  queue_clear; log "Queue cleared."; exit 0 ;;

## Acceptance criteria

* ralph queue add --playlist plan.playlist  appends line to .ralph/queue, prints list
* ralph queue add --max-tasks 5 --scope auth  appends second entry
* ralph queue list  prints numbered list of all entries
* ralph queue next  prints first entry text without modifying file
* ralph queue remove 1  removes first entry, prints updated list
* ralph queue clear  empties .ralph/queue
* Blank lines and # comments in .ralph/queue are skipped by all operations

title: Implement stateless condition evaluators and schedule config/state I/O
description:
## What to implement

Create lib/schedule.sh: stateless condition evaluators, schedule-config and schedule-state
I/O, flock helpers. This is the engine that a periodic tick will call. No wait loops —
every function returns quickly. The OS timer provides cadence; this module provides
decisions and state writing.

## Depends on

ralph-yui.1 (claude-usage --available N flag — CLOSED).

## File to create

lib/schedule.sh (NEW). Add to lib/loader.sh: source "$LIB_DIR/schedule.sh" (after queue.sh).

## Paths (add to lib/config.sh)

* SCHEDULE_CONFIG=".ralph/schedule-config"
* SCHEDULE_STATE=".ralph/schedule-state"
* SCHEDULE_LOCK=".ralph/schedule.lock"
* SCHEDULE_LOG=".ralph/logs/scheduler.log"
* SCHEDULE_TICK_INTERVAL_DEFAULT=300  # seconds (5 min)

## schedule-config format

Plain key=value file (sourced by bash). Written by 'ralph schedule install' /
'ralph schedule reconfigure'. Example:

  SCHEDULE_AT=22:00
  SCHEDULE_STOP_AT=06:00
  SCHEDULE_USAGE_MIN=40
  SCHEDULE_TICK_INTERVAL=300

Missing keys mean "no constraint" (AT/STOP_AT empty, USAGE_MIN=0).

## schedule-state format

Plain key=value file, rewritten atomically every tick (write to tmp, mv):

  status=idle|waiting|running
  waiting_for=usage>=40 | time>=22:00 | (empty when idle/running)
  queue_depth=3
  current_entry=--playlist plan.playlist  (empty unless status=running)
  last_tick=2026-04-15T22:05:03Z
  last_tick_result=ran|skipped-conditions|skipped-empty-queue|skipped-locked|error
  last_run_entry=--max-tasks 5 --scope auth  (empty until first run)
  last_run_exit=0                              (last completed entry's exit code)
  last_run_at=2026-04-15T22:10:12Z

Atomic rewrite rule: always 'mv' from tmp to final, never partial writes. Observers
(tmux statusbar) reading this file must never see half-written state.

## lib/schedule.sh functions

### Config / state I/O

schedule_config_read() — sources SCHEDULE_CONFIG if present. Applies defaults for
  missing keys (AT/STOP_AT empty, USAGE_MIN=0, TICK_INTERVAL=300). No-ops if config
  file missing.

schedule_config_write() — takes keyword pairs (AT=..., STOP_AT=..., USAGE_MIN=...,
  TICK_INTERVAL=...), writes canonical config file. Creates parent dir if needed.

schedule_state_write() — takes keyword pairs, merges with existing state (preserves
  keys not passed), atomically replaces SCHEDULE_STATE via tmp + mv.

schedule_state_read_key KEY — prints value of one key from state file (helper for
  external scripts; statusbar users can grep the file directly too).

### Condition evaluators (all stateless, fast, no sleeps)

condition_start_time_met() — returns 0 if SCHEDULE_AT is empty OR current HHMM >=
  SCHEDULE_AT HHMM. Handles midnight crossing: if AT=22:00 and current is 02:00,
  treat as 'after AT' (the previous day's 22:00 window is still active).

condition_stop_time_passed() — returns 0 if SCHEDULE_STOP_AT is set AND current HHMM
  >= STOP_AT HHMM within the active window. When this returns 0, all_conditions_met
  returns 1 (we're past the cutoff, do not start new entries).

condition_usage_available() — returns 0 if SCHEDULE_USAGE_MIN == 0 OR
  'claude-usage --available $SCHEDULE_USAGE_MIN' exits 0.

all_conditions_met() — AND of: condition_start_time_met AND NOT
  condition_stop_time_passed AND condition_usage_available. On failure, echoes a
  single-line reason string suitable for schedule-state 'waiting_for' key.

### Utilities

seed_usage_data_if_needed() — if 'claude-usage --5-hour' returns null, fire a
  minimal haiku ping to seed the API. Logged to SCHEDULE_LOG. Called opportunistically
  by condition_usage_available before it fails the first time.

with_schedule_lock CMD... — flock SCHEDULE_LOCK in non-blocking mode. If held, log
  'tick skipped: lock held' and return 1. Otherwise run CMD and return its exit code.
  This is the wrapper 'ralph schedule tick' uses around its whole body.

format_hhmm STRING — 'HH:MM' -> integer HHMM for comparison. Handles '9:00' and '09:00'.

now_hhmm() — date +%H%M as integer.

## Why no wait loops

This module never sleeps beyond sub-second operations. Every function returns within
milliseconds. The OS timer (installed by ralph-yui.5) provides cadence by calling
'ralph schedule tick' every SCHEDULE_TICK_INTERVAL seconds. Each tick is independent;
there is no in-memory state to preserve across invocations. Crash recovery is trivial
because there is nothing to recover.

## Acceptance criteria

* schedule_config_read with no file sets defaults (USAGE_MIN=0, etc.)
* schedule_config_write then schedule_config_read round-trips all keys
* schedule_state_write is atomic (no observer ever sees partial content — verify
  by running tail -f in one shell and repeated writes in another)
* condition_start_time_met returns 0 when AT is empty
* condition_start_time_met with AT=22:00 at 02:00 returns 0 (midnight crossing)
* condition_stop_time_passed with STOP_AT just past returns 0
* condition_usage_available with USAGE_MIN=0 returns 0 without calling claude-usage
* condition_usage_available with USAGE_MIN=99 returns 1 (never that free)
* all_conditions_met echoes the failing condition's reason string on failure
* with_schedule_lock serializes correctly: second concurrent call exits 1 immediately
* seed_usage_data_if_needed is a no-op when --5-hour returns non-null

## Non-goals

This bead does NOT implement: the 'ralph schedule tick' subcommand (that is in
ralph-yui.5, which glues these evaluators to queue + entry execution), the OS unit
file templates, or the install/uninstall flow.

      [[ -n "$SCHEDULE_AT" ]]          && FORWARD_ARGS+=(--at "$SCHEDULE_AT")
