title: ralph schedule subcommand: install/tick/status surface + OS unit templates
description:
## What to implement

The 'ralph schedule' subcommand with full install/uninstall/tick/status/logs/attach/
reconfigure verbs, plus launchd plist and systemd user unit/timer templates. This is
the glue between lib/schedule.sh evaluators (ralph-yui.3), lib/queue.sh (ralph-yui.2),
and the host OS scheduler.

## Architecture recap

* OS timer (launchd StartInterval on darwin, systemd .timer on linux) fires
  'ralph schedule tick' every SCHEDULE_TICK_INTERVAL seconds.
* Each tick is stateless and one-shot: acquire flock, evaluate conditions, maybe pop
  one queue entry and run it synchronously, write schedule-state, release lock, exit.
* Schedule parameters live in .ralph/schedule-config (readable/writable across ticks).
* No long-running scheduler daemon exists anywhere.

## Depends on

* ralph-yui.2 (queue subcommand + queue_remove_first)
* ralph-yui.3 (schedule.sh evaluators, config/state I/O, with_schedule_lock)
* ralph-yui.4 (build_forward_args with --playlist + schedule flags, sync_schedule_state_files)

## Files to create/modify

* lib/args.sh — 'schedule' subcommand with nested verbs (install|uninstall|tick|
  status|logs|attach|reconfigure)
* lib/schedule_install.sh (NEW) — OS unit generation + load/unload, platform detection
* lib/schedule.sh — add run_schedule_tick, run_schedule_status (stays small; heavy
  lifting is in _install.sh and existing ralph-yui.3 evaluators)
* lib/remote.sh — add run_remote_schedule_install (uses sync_schedule_state_files
  from ralph-yui.4, then SSHes to run 'ralph schedule install' on remote)
* lib/loader.sh — source schedule_install.sh after schedule.sh
* templates/launchd-scheduler.plist — launchd agent template (darwin)
* templates/systemd-scheduler.service — systemd user service (linux)
* templates/systemd-scheduler.timer — systemd user timer (linux)
* templates/usage.txt — document 'ralph schedule' verbs

## CLI surface

ralph schedule install [--at HH:MM] [--stop-at HH:MM] [--usage-available N]
                       [--tick-interval SECONDS] [-r HOST]
    Writes .ralph/schedule-config from flags, generates platform-appropriate OS unit,
    loads it. With -r: syncs config + queue to remote, SSHes and runs install there.
    Idempotent: re-running replaces config and reloads unit.

ralph schedule uninstall [-r HOST]
    Unloads OS unit and removes unit file. Does NOT delete .ralph/schedule-config
    or .ralph/queue (they survive uninstall). With -r: runs uninstall on remote.

ralph schedule reconfigure [--at HH:MM] [--stop-at HH:MM] [--usage-available N]
                           [--tick-interval SECONDS]
    Updates .ralph/schedule-config only. If TICK_INTERVAL changed, regenerates and
    reloads the unit file. Otherwise leaves OS unit untouched.

ralph schedule tick
    One-shot. What the OS timer calls. Acquires flock; reads config; evaluates
    conditions via all_conditions_met; if met and queue non-empty, pops head entry
    and runs 'ralph $entry' synchronously, then queue_remove_first on success;
    writes schedule-state; releases lock; exits. Always exits 0 except on internal
    error. Designed to be safe to run manually for testing.

ralph schedule status
    Prints .ralph/schedule-config, .ralph/schedule-state, queue depth, OS unit
    status (launchctl print / systemctl --user status), path to log file.
    Non-zero exit if unit not loaded.

ralph schedule logs [-n N] [-f]
    tail -n N SCHEDULE_LOG, optional -f. Do not default to follow mode.

ralph schedule attach
    If a tick has launched a ralph entry inside a named tmux session (the tick wraps
    the inner ralph in 'tmux new-session -d -s ralph-entry ...'), attach to it.
    Else print 'no active entry' and exit 1.

## run_schedule_tick (lib/schedule.sh)

run_schedule_tick() {
  schedule_config_read
  with_schedule_lock _do_tick
}

_do_tick() {
  local reason
  local depth
  depth=$(queue_count)
  schedule_state_write last_tick="$(now_iso)"

  if (( depth == 0 )); then
    schedule_state_write status=idle waiting_for="" queue_depth=0 \
                         last_tick_result=skipped-empty-queue
    return 0
  fi

  if ! reason=$(all_conditions_met); then
    schedule_state_write status=waiting waiting_for="$reason" queue_depth="$depth" \
                         last_tick_result=skipped-conditions
    return 0
  fi

  local entry
  entry=$(queue_next)
  schedule_state_write status=running current_entry="$entry" queue_depth="$depth" \
                       waiting_for="" last_tick_result=ran
  local exit_code=0
  # shellcheck disable=SC2086
  "$SCRIPT_DIR/ralph" $entry >>"$SCHEDULE_LOG" 2>&1 || exit_code=$?
  if (( exit_code == 0 )); then
    queue_remove_first
  fi
  schedule_state_write status=idle current_entry="" \
                       queue_depth="$(queue_count)" \
                       last_run_entry="$entry" last_run_exit="$exit_code" \
                       last_run_at="$(now_iso)"
}

Note the lock is held for the entire ralph invocation — possibly hours. That is
intentional: it serializes tick concurrency against in-flight entry execution
without needing separate PID tracking. Subsequent ticks during a long entry
fast-exit via with_schedule_lock.

## Install flow (lib/schedule_install.sh)

detect_platform() — echoes 'darwin' or 'linux'. Errors on unsupported.

install_schedule_unit() {
  case $(detect_platform) in
    darwin) install_launchd_unit ;;
    linux)  install_systemd_unit ;;
  esac
}

install_launchd_unit() — renders templates/launchd-scheduler.plist via render_template
  with keys RALPH_BIN, WORKING_DIR, TICK_INTERVAL, LOG_FILE. Writes to
  ~/Library/LaunchAgents/dev.ralph.scheduler.<project-hash>.plist. launchctl unload
  (ignore errors) then launchctl load -w. Project-hash in filename allows multiple
  ralph projects to have independent schedulers.

install_systemd_unit() — renders .service + .timer templates with same keys. Writes
  to ~/.config/systemd/user/ralph-scheduler-<project-hash>.{service,timer}. Runs
  systemctl --user daemon-reload, then systemctl --user enable --now
  ralph-scheduler-<project-hash>.timer.

uninstall_schedule_unit() — symmetric: launchctl unload + rm plist, or
  systemctl --user disable --now + rm unit files + daemon-reload.

project_hash() — short hash of absolute project path, used to namespace unit names
  so multiple ralph projects coexist.

## launchd plist template (templates/launchd-scheduler.plist)

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "...">
<plist version="1.0">
<dict>
    <key>Label</key>                      <string>dev.ralph.scheduler.{{PROJECT_HASH}}</string>
    <key>ProgramArguments</key>
    <array>
        <string>{{RALPH_BIN}}</string>
        <string>schedule</string>
        <string>tick</string>
    </array>
    <key>WorkingDirectory</key>           <string>{{WORKING_DIR}}</string>
    <key>StartInterval</key>              <integer>{{TICK_INTERVAL}}</integer>
    <key>StandardOutPath</key>            <string>{{LOG_FILE}}</string>
    <key>StandardErrorPath</key>          <string>{{LOG_FILE}}</string>
    <key>RunAtLoad</key>                  <false/>
</dict>
</plist>

## systemd templates

templates/systemd-scheduler.service:
    [Unit]
    Description=Ralph scheduler tick ({{WORKING_DIR}})
    [Service]
    Type=oneshot
    WorkingDirectory={{WORKING_DIR}}
    ExecStart={{RALPH_BIN}} schedule tick
    StandardOutput=append:{{LOG_FILE}}
    StandardError=append:{{LOG_FILE}}

templates/systemd-scheduler.timer:
    [Unit]
    Description=Ralph scheduler tick timer ({{WORKING_DIR}})
    [Timer]
    OnBootSec=1min
    OnUnitActiveSec={{TICK_INTERVAL}}s
    AccuracySec=15s
    Persistent=true
    [Install]
    WantedBy=timers.target

## Remote install (lib/remote.sh)

run_remote_schedule_install() {
  sync_ralph                        # existing helper
  sync_schedule_state_files         # from ralph-yui.4: queue + schedule-config
  local forward_args
  forward_args=$(build_forward_args_for schedule install)
  ssh "$REMOTE_HOST" "cd $REMOTE_DIR && ~/.ralph/ralph schedule install $forward_args"
}

Similar run_remote_schedule_uninstall, run_remote_schedule_status (greps remote's
.ralph/schedule-state over SSH).

## args.sh integration

In parse_arg_flags, after existing subcommands:

  schedule)
    case "${2:-}" in
      install)     ACTION="schedule_install";     shift 2 ;;
      uninstall)   ACTION="schedule_uninstall";   shift 2 ;;
      reconfigure) ACTION="schedule_reconfigure"; shift 2 ;;
      tick)        ACTION="schedule_tick";        shift 2 ;;
      status)      ACTION="schedule_status";      shift 2 ;;
      logs)        ACTION="schedule_logs";        shift 2 ;;
      attach)      ACTION="schedule_attach";      shift 2 ;;
      *) log "ERROR: ralph schedule {install|uninstall|reconfigure|tick|status|logs|attach}"; exit 1 ;;
    esac
    ;;

Schedule flags (--at, --stop-at, --usage-available, --tick-interval) parsed by the
existing flag cases from ralph-yui.3 args.sh changes.

In dispatch_early_exit_action, dispatch each schedule_* ACTION. For install/uninstall/
reconfigure, if REMOTE_MODE=true call the run_remote_schedule_* variant instead.

## Acceptance criteria

* ralph schedule install --at 22:00 --usage-available 40 --tick-interval 300
  writes .ralph/schedule-config with the three values, generates and loads launchd
  plist (darwin) or systemd user unit (linux), returns 0
* launchctl list | grep ralph.scheduler (darwin) OR systemctl --user list-timers
  (linux) shows the unit active after install
* ralph schedule status shows config, state, queue depth, OS unit active/inactive
* ralph schedule tick with empty queue sets schedule-state status=idle,
  last_tick_result=skipped-empty-queue, exits 0
* ralph schedule tick with queue entry but usage below threshold sets status=waiting,
  waiting_for contains the reason, entry remains in queue
* ralph schedule tick with all conditions met and one queue entry: runs it,
  removes from queue, schedule-state shows last_run_exit=0
* Two concurrent 'ralph schedule tick' invocations: second fast-exits on lock without
  running anything
* ralph schedule uninstall unloads unit and removes unit file; .ralph/schedule-config
  and .ralph/queue are preserved
* ralph schedule reconfigure --usage-available 60 updates config only; unit file
  unchanged (unless TICK_INTERVAL changed, in which case it regenerates)
* ralph schedule install -r oracle --at 22:00 syncs queue + schedule-config to oracle,
  SSHes and installs systemd user unit on oracle
* Multiple ralph projects on one host have independent scheduler units
  (project_hash namespacing)

## Non-goals

Does not implement the tmux statusbar integration itself — that is user-side
consumption of .ralph/schedule-state. This bead guarantees schedule-state exists
and is atomically updated on every tick.
